notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The Quran asks about the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, who said to a prophet of theirs, appoint a king for us so that we may fight in the way of God.

He asked whether, if fighting were decreed for them, they might not fight, and they asked why they should not fight in the way of God when they had been driven out from their homes and from their children, but when fighting was decreed for them, they turned back, except a few of them, and God knows the wrongdoers.

chapters.summary_md: After Musa, the chiefs of the Children of Israel asked a prophet of theirs to appoint a king so that they might fight in the way of God [c1]. When fighting was decreed for them, they turned back, except a few of them [c2].
chapters.body_md: The Quran asks about the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, who said to a prophet of theirs, appoint a king for us so that we may fight in the way of God [c1]. He asked whether, if fighting were decreed for them, they might not fight, and they asked why they should not fight in the way of God when they had been driven out from their homes and from their children, but when fighting was decreed for them, they turned back, except a few of them, and God knows the wrongdoers [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name the prophet or the chiefs [c1]. It reports the prophet's doubt that they would fight, and their answer that they had been driven from their homes and children [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The chiefs of the Children of Israel asked a prophet of theirs to appoint a king [c1]. When fighting was decreed, they turned back, except a few of them [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets the chiefs' words beside what they did when fighting was decreed [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the prophet's name, the chiefs' names, or the time and place. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the prophet is given a name in later works.
- Not established: who drove them out of their homes.
- Not established: how many turned back, or how many stayed.

claims.statement_en: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king for them, and they asked how he could have kingship over them when they were more deserving of it than he, and he had not been given abundance of wealth.
He said that God had chosen him over them and increased him in knowledge and in body, and that God gives His kingship to whom He wills.

Their prophet told them that the sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them, with tranquillity from their Lord in it and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun had left, carried by the angels, and the ayah says that in this is a sign for them if they are believers.

chapters.summary_md: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king for them [c1]. He said that God had chosen him over them and increased him in knowledge and in body [c2]. The sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them [c3].
chapters.body_md: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king for them, and they asked how he could have kingship over them when they were more deserving of it than he, and he had not been given abundance of wealth [c1]. He said that God had chosen him over them and increased him in knowledge and in body, and that God gives His kingship to whom He wills [c2]. Their prophet told them that the sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them, with tranquillity from their Lord in it and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun had left, carried by the angels, and the ayah says that in this is a sign for them if they are believers [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The objection in the ayah is about wealth and about who was more deserving of kingship [c1]. The reply gives God's choice and knowledge and body as the reasons [c2]. The ayat say what the chest contains but not what became of it [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king [c1]. They asked how he could be king [c1]. He said that God had chosen him and increased him in knowledge [c2]. The sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the prophet answers the objection about wealth by pointing to God's choice and to knowledge [c1][c2]. Another is that the chest is given as a sign for those who believe [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Talut's lineage, his age or what he did before; the ayah gives only the name.
- Not established: what the chest was, where it came from, or what the remnant was.
- Not established: what increased in body means in detail.

claims.statement_en: When Talut set out with the forces, he said that God would test them with a river, so that whoever drank from it was not of him, and whoever did not taste it was of him, except one who scooped a handful with his hand, and they drank from it, except a few of them.

When he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said that they had no strength that day against Jalut and his forces, but those who were certain that they would meet God said that many a small group has overcome a large group by God's permission, and that God is with the patient.
When they went out against Jalut and his forces, they said, our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm and help us against the disbelieving people.
They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut, and God gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed.
The ayah adds that, were it not for God's repelling of people, some by others, the earth would be corrupted, but God is possessor of bounty over the worlds.
God says that these are His signs, which He recites to the listener in truth, and that the listener is among the messengers.

chapters.summary_md: Talut told his forces that God would test them with a river [c1]. When they met Jalut and his forces, they asked God to pour patience upon them [c3]. They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut [c4].
chapters.body_md: When Talut set out with the forces, he said that God would test them with a river, so that whoever drank from it was not of him, and whoever did not taste it was of him, except one who scooped a handful with his hand, and they drank from it, except a few of them [c1]. When he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said that they had no strength that day against Jalut and his forces, but those who were certain that they would meet God said that many a small group has overcome a large group by God's permission, and that God is with the patient [c2]. When they went out against Jalut and his forces, they said, our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm and help us against the disbelieving people [c3]. They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut, and God gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed [c4]. The ayah adds that, were it not for God's repelling of people, some by others, the earth would be corrupted, but God is possessor of bounty over the worlds [c5]. God says that these are His signs, which He recites to the listener in truth, and that the listener is among the messengers [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not say how many drank and how many did not [c1]. It gives the words of those who had no strength that day, and the answer of those who were certain they would meet God [c2]. It names Dawud only in the verse about the defeat of Jalut [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Talut told his forces that God would test them with a river [c1]. When they met Jalut and his forces, they asked God to pour patience upon them [c3]. They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets the words of those who had no strength that day beside the words of those who were certain they would meet God [c2]. Another is that the victory is attributed to God's permission [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how many were in the forces, how many drank, or where the river was.
- Not established: how Dawud killed Jalut, or how old Dawud was.
- Not established: Jalut's origin or his people. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Talut and Jalut are matched with figures of earlier scriptures, and the numbers of those who crossed the river are given in later works.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the prophet, Talut's lineage and the numbers of the forces are given in later works, and Talut and Jalut are matched with figures of earlier scriptures.
Hadith to add later: reports about the forces who crossed the river, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
